boards.school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Hunt Library spaces for quiet work, group projects, making, data work, and campus events.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor
cards.notes: Bring reading or solo work and use the large tables; the Libraries designates this space for no talking.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled, no-talking room with large study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries identifies the Quiet Reading Room on Hunt Library’s second floor and lists its sound level as “No talking.”
cards.source_title: Quiet Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | Explore Spaces
cards.access_notes: Located past the library gates on Hunt Library’s second floor; follow the Libraries’ posted directions.

cards.title: Rain Garden Reading Lounge
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor
cards.notes: Use the second-floor reading lounge as a named stop while exploring Hunt’s study areas and floor layout.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed reading lounge beside Hunt’s rain garden.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ Hunt Library directory and floor map list the Rain Garden Reading Lounge on the second floor.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library Room Directory | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Consult the Hunt Library floor map for its current placement and building access.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Third Floor
cards.notes: Meet collaborators or set up individual work in the third-floor commons; check the map for nearby workstations.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Hunt Library commons with computer workstations nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ Hunt Library map lists the Learning Commons and computer workstations on the third floor.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library Map | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Enter Hunt Library and use the posted floor map to reach Floor 3.

cards.title: Lake Raleigh Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when you need a mapped commons area; confirm available computers or seating on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor learning commons at Hunt Library.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ Hunt Library directory lists Lake Raleigh Learning Commons on the fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library Room Directory | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the Hunt Library floor map for current wayfinding and any space-specific restrictions.

cards.title: The Landing
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Third Floor
cards.notes: Pause here between classes or work sessions; locate it from the third-floor map opposite the Dataspace.
cards.short_summary: A named third-floor Hunt Library space near the Dataspace.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries lists The Landing on Hunt Library’s third floor; its Dataspace directions place Dataspace opposite The Landing.
cards.source_title: Dataspace, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | Explore Spaces
cards.access_notes: Follow Hunt Library’s third-floor map; Dataspace directions identify The Landing as the nearby landmark.

cards.title: Skyline Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fifth Floor
cards.notes: Make the fifth-floor reading room a destination for a change of setting, then check the adjacent floor map.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room at the top level of Hunt Library.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ Hunt Library map and directory list the Skyline Reading Room on the fifth floor.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library Map | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use elevators or stairs to Floor 5 and consult the posted Hunt floor map.

cards.title: Maker Studio
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Complete the required online orientation before planning a 3D-printing session in Hunt’s Maker Studio.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor making space with orientation-based 3D-print access.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries lists the Maker Studio on Hunt Library’s fourth floor and requires a brief online orientation for 3D-printing access there.
cards.source_title: 3D Printing | Think and Do at the Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: 3D printers are for current NC State students, staff, and faculty with valid Campus ID after the required orientation.

cards.title: Dataspace
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Third Floor
cards.notes: Use the data desktops for specialized software work, and ask library staff for help with data questions.
cards.short_summary: A data-focused room with Mac, Windows, and Linux desktops.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes Dataspace as a place for the NC State community to use powerful computers and specialized data software.
cards.source_title: Dataspace, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | Explore Spaces
cards.access_notes: Located on Floor 3 opposite The Landing; workstation access and reservations may have current requirements.

cards.title: Lenovo Esports and Gaming Lab
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Find the fourth-floor gaming lab from the directory before arranging a campus-appropriate game or technology session.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor gaming and esports lab in Hunt Library.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ Hunt Library directory lists the Lenovo Esports and Gaming Lab in room 4403 on the fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library Room Directory | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check current lab availability, equipment policies, and any campus-ID requirements before visiting.

cards.title: iPearl Immersion Theater
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor
cards.notes: Use the floor map to locate the theater and look for scheduled academic presentations or other approved programming.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor immersion theater at Hunt Library.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ Hunt Library directory lists the iPearl Immersion Theater on the second floor in room 2206.
cards.source_title: Hunt Library Room Directory | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the Hunt Library floor map and confirm event or room-access arrangements before attending.

boards.school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented, no-admission activities on and near NC State, with optional purchases excluded from the plan.

cards.title: Walk the JC Raulston Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Public garden at NC State, 4415 Beryl Road
cards.notes: Meet at the visitor center, then take a slow loop through the plant collections; bring water and follow garden rules while you explore.
cards.short_summary: A year-round garden walk with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The JC Raulston Arboretum is open to the public year-round at no cost.
cards.source_title: JC Raulston Arboretum Visitor Information
cards.access_notes: Public access; check the visitor-information page for seasonal garden hours and occasional event closures.

cards.title: Join the Sunday garden tour
cards.subtitle: Bobby G. Wilder Visitor Center, JC Raulston Arboretum
cards.notes: Arrive at the visitor center before 2 p.m. and join the volunteer docent for a one-hour walk through the garden’s collections.
cards.short_summary: A free, public guided introduction to the Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Volunteer-led Sunday tours are available to the public free of charge at 2 p.m. from March through October.
cards.source_title: Sunday Tour — JC Raulston Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Sundays at 2 p.m., March–October; no advance registration is available. Meet at the visitor center.

cards.title: Browse the People’s Collection
cards.subtitle: NC Museum of Art, East and West buildings
cards.notes: Pick a gallery wing, compare a few works at your own pace, and skip ticketed special exhibitions to keep the visit completely free.
cards.short_summary: Free access to NCMA’s permanent collection galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the People’s Collection in the NCMA East and West buildings is free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — NCMA Raleigh
cards.access_notes: Galleries are open Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; special exhibitions can require a paid ticket.

cards.entity_name: Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park
cards.title: Walk art trails at Museum Park
cards.subtitle: NC Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Road
cards.notes: Start at the Welcome Center, choose a trail, and pause at outdoor installations; stay on open paths and plan to finish before dusk.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor art-and-nature walk beside NC State.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park is free and open daily, including holidays, from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: Museum Park — NCMA Raleigh
cards.access_notes: Public park access is free from dawn to dusk; check the trail-closures notice before leaving.

cards.title: Take an NCMA guided park walk
cards.subtitle: Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park
cards.notes: Reserve a spot for an available themed walk, then meet ready to cover the park on foot while discussing art, nature, or sustainability.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled, no-cost guided walk through Museum Park.
cards.evidence_claim: NCMA’s guided Museum Park tours are free, though space is limited and preregistration is required.
cards.source_title: Tours — NCMA Raleigh
cards.access_notes: Scheduled monthly in April, May, June, September, October, and November; preregistration is required and tours are for ages 12+.

cards.entity_name: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
cards.title: Explore the science museum
cards.subtitle: Downtown Raleigh, 11 West Jones Street
cards.notes: Choose a few exhibit floors, compare notes on a favorite specimen or display, and avoid paid 3D films or special exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown museum visit centered on natural science.
cards.evidence_claim: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences offers free general admission.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
cards.access_notes: Downtown museum hours are Monday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; verify listed holiday closures before visiting.

cards.title: Catch a Pullen Park concert
cards.subtitle: Pullen Park event lawn, 520 Ashe Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or chair and settle in for the outdoor set; skip café purchases and check the city listing for weather changes.
cards.short_summary: A current free summer music series at Pullen Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Raleigh’s 2026 Pullen and Fletcher Park Summer Concert Series is free, with Pullen Park dates listed through August 16.
cards.source_title: 2026 Summer Concert Series — City of Raleigh
cards.access_notes: Select Sunday evenings, 6–8 p.m.; this seasonal series may change or be canceled, so confirm the current listing first.

cards.title: Bring a blanket for Pullen movie night
cards.subtitle: Pullen Park event lawn, 520 Ashe Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a lawn chair or blanket, arrive before the screening, and enjoy the outdoor film without buying refreshments from the café.
cards.short_summary: Free outdoor movie screenings scheduled through October.
cards.evidence_claim: Pullen Park Movie Series screenings are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Movie Series at Pullen Park — City of Raleigh
cards.access_notes: First Tuesday of each month through October; screenings are weather-dependent and the city posts cancellation updates.

cards.entity_name: D. H. Hill Jr. Library Exhibit Gallery
cards.title: See the D. H. Hill exhibit gallery
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, 2 Broughton Drive
cards.notes: Meet in the east-wing gallery, read the exhibit labels together, and use the library’s current-hours page before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus exhibition stop with publicly accessible displays.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries’ east-wing D. H. Hill exhibit gallery presents ongoing exhibitions that are free of charge and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Exhibit Program Guidelines — NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open during D. H. Hill Jr. Library hours, with occasional closures for installation or maintenance.

cards.title: Browse Hunt Library’s exhibit spaces
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library, 1070 Partners Way
cards.notes: Choose a display wall or physical exhibit space, take time with the work, and check building access information before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing NC State library stop for rotating displays.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State University Libraries states that its buildings and physical and digital exhibit spaces are open to the public every day.
cards.source_title: Strategic Priorities — NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Public exhibit access is described by the Libraries; consult current building hours before visiting.

boards.school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study settings across NC State’s D. H. Hill Jr. and James B. Hunt Jr. Libraries, spanning silent reading rooms, collaborative areas, and computer-equipped commons.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor
cards.notes: Settle into a no-talking room with large reading tables and controllable lighting; enter through the gap between the second-floor study-room blocks.
cards.short_summary: A silent, light-filled reading room with large tables.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes the Hunt Quiet Reading Room as a tranquil, light-filled study and reflection space with large tables and a no-talking sound level.
cards.source_title: Quiet Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, second floor; the library directs visitors through the library gates and past the elevator bay. Check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Skyline Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fifth Floor
cards.notes: Use the fifth-floor tables, soft seating, and standing-height table when you want a silent setting with natural light and Lake Raleigh-facing views.
cards.short_summary: A fifth-floor silent room with natural light and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries states that the Skyline Reading Room has reading tables, soft seating, abundant natural light, views, and a no-talking sound level.
cards.source_title: Skyline Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, fifth floor. Check current library hours and building access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Oval View Reading Room
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Bring an individual task to the fourth-floor room, which combines lounge seats, work tables, natural light, and a hushed-voices setting overlooking the Oval.
cards.short_summary: Hushed fourth-floor seating overlooking the Oval.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries documents lounge seating, work tables, natural light, hushed voices, and views over Hunt Library and the Centennial Campus Oval.
cards.source_title: Oval View Reading Room, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, fourth floor; the library provides elevator and stair directions from the entrance. Check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Lake Raleigh Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Fourth Floor
cards.notes: Choose a computer workstation or collaborative table in this fourth-floor commons, where three walls of windows bring in daylight and Lake Raleigh views.
cards.short_summary: A computer-equipped commons with three-sided floor-to-ceiling windows.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes computer workstations for individual and collaborative work, colorful furniture, floor-to-ceiling windows on three sides, and Lake Raleigh views.
cards.source_title: Lake Raleigh Learning Commons, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, fourth floor. The listed equipment includes Mac, Windows, and Linux Engineering desktops; check current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Idea Alcove
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Second Floor · Room 2302
cards.notes: Use the movable furniture and wall-sized whiteboard for an impromptu working session near the Quiet Reading Room; keep voices appropriate for an active space.
cards.short_summary: An informal collaboration area with mobile furniture and a full-wall whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries identifies the Idea Alcove as an open, informal collaboration space with movable furniture, large tables, lockers, and a whiteboard covering the north wall.
cards.source_title: Idea Alcove, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, second floor, Room 2302, near the Quiet Reading Room. This space is listed with conversation-and-chatter sound level; check current library hours.

cards.title: Study Room 3315
cards.subtitle: James B. Hunt Jr. Library · Third Floor
cards.notes: Reserve this six-person room for a focused group session; it has a work table, whiteboard, controllable white-noise speaker, and overlooks the Quiet Reading Room.
cards.short_summary: A reservable six-person group room overlooking the Quiet Reading Room.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries lists Study Room 3315 as a six-person room with a work table, whiteboard, controllable white-noise speaker, and student/faculty/staff reservations up to seven days ahead.
cards.source_title: Study Room 3315, James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Hunt Library, third floor. Reservable up to seven days in advance for up to two hours by students, graduate students, faculty, and staff; a 15-minute arrival grace period applies.

cards.title: Hill Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · First Floor, West Wing · Rooms 1325 and 1311
cards.notes: For individual silent work, use the glass-walled room’s work tables and picture-window views toward the terrace and Brickyard; no talking is permitted.
cards.short_summary: A glass-separated silent room with Brickyard-facing windows.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes Hill’s Quiet Reading Room as individual silent-study space, isolated from ambient noise by a glass wall, with work tables and no talking.
cards.source_title: Quiet Reading Room, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, first floor West Wing, Rooms 1325 and 1311. The library provides routes from Brickyard and Hillsborough Street entrances; check current hours.

cards.title: Ground Floor Reading Room
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · Ground Floor, Tower
cards.notes: Spread out at a large table or choose lounge seating in this traditional library-style reading room; the circulating DVD collection is also housed here.
cards.short_summary: A large traditional reading room with tables and lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries calls the Ground Floor Reading Room a large study space with traditional library-style seating, lounge seating, and large tables.
cards.source_title: Ground Floor Reading Room, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, ground-floor Tower. Check current library hours and access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: North Forum
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · Third Floor, Tower
cards.notes: Set up a collaborative session at the configurable large work tables and whiteboards just north of the Visualization Studio; this is a conversation-and-chatter area.
cards.short_summary: An open third-floor work area with configurable tables and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries describes the North Forum as an open study area north of the Visualization Studio with large configurable work tables and whiteboards.
cards.source_title: North Forum, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, third-floor Tower, north of the Visualization Studio. Listed sound level is conversation and chatter; check current library hours.

cards.title: Study Lounge 2301
cards.subtitle: D. H. Hill Jr. Library · Second Floor, West Wing · Room 2301
cards.notes: Take a casual study break at a booth or table in this naturally lit lounge, which also has a whiteboard and nearby food and drink vending machines.
cards.short_summary: A naturally lit lounge with booth seating, tables, and a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Libraries lists Study Lounge 2301 as a study space with casual booth seating, tables and chairs, natural light, a whiteboard, and vending machines.
cards.source_title: Study Lounge 2301, D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: D. H. Hill Jr. Library, second-floor West Wing, Room 2301. The library provides routes from the Brickyard entrance; check current library hours before visiting.

boards.school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on Hillsborough Street and nearby connecting corridors, each with one source-backed reason to stop.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for free art
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 1903 Hillsborough Street
cards.notes: Check the current exhibitions, then use the museum’s public hours to plan a self-guided visit; admission is listed as free.
cards.short_summary: A public art museum at the Hillsborough Street edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gregg Museum is at 1903 Hillsborough Street, is open to the public, and has free admission.
cards.source_title: Visit | Gregg Museum of Art + Design
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm special closures before going.

cards.title: Ashe Avenue for park time
cards.subtitle: Ashe Avenue beside the Hillsborough Street corridor — 520 Ashe Avenue
cards.notes: Use the city’s park map to choose a playground, court, field, arts, or theatre stop; rides require separate tickets.
cards.short_summary: A City of Raleigh park with recreation areas and optional amusement rides.
cards.evidence_claim: Pullen Park is at 520 Ashe Avenue and offers playgrounds, courts and fields, arts, theatre, and ticketed rides.
cards.source_title: Pullen Park | Raleighnc.gov
cards.access_notes: The park and restrooms are listed open daily 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; ride availability varies.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for coffee and biscuits
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 2100 Hillsborough Street, Suite 100
cards.notes: Use the posted Hillsborough location and menu to plan a coffee, sweet biscuit, waffle, or sandwich stop.
cards.short_summary: A café at the Belltower end of Hillsborough Street with coffee and food.
cards.evidence_claim: Jubala lists its NCSU Belltower location at 2100 Hillsborough Street and offers coffee, biscuits, waffles, and sandwiches.
cards.source_title: Jubala Coffee Menu
cards.access_notes: Listed Hillsborough hours are 7 a.m.–5 p.m. weekdays and 8 a.m.–5 p.m. weekends.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for organic coffee
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 2428 Hillsborough Street
cards.notes: Use the address to find the café and check its current offerings directly before visiting; the corridor directory lists it as a coffee shop.
cards.short_summary: A named coffee-shop stop along Hillsborough Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hillsborough Street corridor directory lists Global Village Organic Coffee at 2428 Hillsborough Street under coffee shops.
cards.source_title: Coffee Shops | Hillsborough Street
cards.access_notes: Check the business directly for current operating details.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for warm cookies
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 2302 Hillsborough Street, Suite 104
cards.notes: Use the shop’s listed address for a cookie stop, and check its menu or ordering options before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Hillsborough Street cookie shop listed with freshly baked cookie flavors.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies is listed at 2302 Hillsborough Street and offers freshly baked cookies in multiple flavors.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies | Hillsborough Street
cards.access_notes: The corridor listing shows daily hours of 11 a.m.–3 a.m.; verify before a late visit.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for arepas
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 2524 Hillsborough Street
cards.notes: Use the listed address for a quick food stop and review the restaurant’s current menu before choosing what to order.
cards.short_summary: A named fast-casual food stop on Hillsborough Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hillsborough Street corridor directory lists Guasaca at 2524 Hillsborough Street in its food-on-the-go category.
cards.source_title: Food on the Go | Hillsborough Street
cards.access_notes: Check the restaurant directly for current hours and menu availability.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for essentials
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 2512 Hillsborough Street
cards.notes: Use the corridor listing to locate the store when you need everyday items, then check Target directly for in-stock products.
cards.short_summary: A named retail destination on the Hillsborough Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hillsborough Street directory lists Target at 2512 Hillsborough Street.
cards.source_title: Convenience & Grocery | Hillsborough Street
cards.access_notes: Check the retailer directly for current store details and product availability.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for books and records
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 3106 Hillsborough Street
cards.notes: Browse the physical store’s used books and records, or ask about special orders; its site notes a rear lot reached from Daisy Street.
cards.short_summary: A single-location Raleigh book and record store on Hillsborough Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Nice Price Books & Records lists its one Raleigh location at 3106 Hillsborough Street and sells used books and records.
cards.source_title: FAQ | Nice Price Books & Records
cards.access_notes: Its site lists daily hours of 11 a.m.–7 p.m.; check for holiday changes.

cards.title: Hillsborough Street for an early coffee stop
cards.subtitle: Hillsborough Street corridor — 3100 Hillsborough Street
cards.notes: Use the Hillsborough location for coffee and check the café’s posted daily hours before starting an early errand or study break.
cards.short_summary: A coffee-shop location with daily hours beginning at 6 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Cup A Joe lists its Hillsborough Street location at 3100 Hillsborough Street and daily hours of 6 a.m.–7 p.m.
cards.source_title: Contact | Cup A Joe
cards.access_notes: Listed as open seven days a week, 6 a.m.–7 p.m.; verify changes directly.

cards.title: Beryl Road for a free garden walk
cards.subtitle: Beryl Road corridor, near Hillsborough Street — 4415 Beryl Road
cards.notes: Enter during the posted garden hours and explore the living plant collection; review event notices because special programs can affect access.
cards.short_summary: A public NC State garden and living laboratory with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The JC Raulston Arboretum is at 4415 Beryl Road, open to the public year-round, and has free admission.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | JC Raulston Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Garden hours vary seasonally; the official visitor page notes occasional event-related schedule changes.

boards.school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented NC State traditions spanning campus expression, Wolfpack ceremonies, music, mascots and homecoming.

cards.title: Paint the Free Expression Tunnel
cards.subtitle: A student canvas beneath the rail tracks
cards.notes: Walk through the tunnel’s changing messages, then add a lawful, respectful design when campus guidelines and paint access allow.
cards.short_summary: A continually repainted public-expression tradition dating to the 1960s.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State describes the Free Expression Tunnel as an outlet for student creativity and expression since the 1960s.
cards.source_title: Get Oriented With the NC State Bucket List
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian tunnel; follow posted campus policies and use only permitted materials.

cards.title: Leave a Handprint for Respect the Pack
cards.subtitle: Free Expression Tunnel during Wolfpack Welcome Weeks
cards.notes: During the annual Respect the Pack event, add your handprint to the mural near the tunnel entrance and read its inclusion message.
cards.short_summary: An annual handprint ritual supporting a campus culture of respect.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State says every student is invited to paint a handprint on the mural at the annual Respect the Pack event during Wolfpack Welcome Weeks.
cards.source_title: Get Oriented With the NC State Bucket List
cards.access_notes: Available during the scheduled Respect the Pack event; check Wolfpack Welcome Weeks programming.

cards.title: See the Memorial Belltower Lit Red
cards.subtitle: Memorial Belltower celebration tradition
cards.notes: Check university or athletics announcements after major Wolfpack achievements, then view the Belltower’s red illumination from public campus space.
cards.short_summary: The Belltower’s red lighting marks celebrated Wolfpack accomplishments.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State identifies lighting the Memorial Belltower red as a way the university celebrates athletics wins and faculty achievements.
cards.source_title: Red and White Week
cards.access_notes: Illumination occurs for selected achievements; it is visible from public outdoor areas.

cards.title: Turn the Block S Outward at Graduation
cards.subtitle: NC State commencement tradition
cards.notes: Eligible students can learn the ring symbols, wear the Block S inward before graduation, then turn it outward at commencement.
cards.short_summary: The ring orientation changes from student journey to alumni accomplishment.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Alumni states students wear the Block S inward and turn it outward during university commencement after graduating.
cards.source_title: NC State Ring
cards.access_notes: Ring eligibility requires 60 undergraduate credits or graduate enrollment; purchasing a ring is optional.

cards.entity_name: Fellowship of the Ring at the Belltower
cards.title: Let a Class Ring Spend a Night in the Belltower
cards.subtitle: Memorial Belltower Shrine Room ceremony
cards.notes: If receiving an NC State ring, register for the Fellowship ceremony and collect it at the following Celebration of Pack Traditions.
cards.short_summary: Class rings are placed overnight in the Belltower’s Shrine Room.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Alumni says participants may have their ring spend a night in the Memorial Belltower Shrine Room before it is presented the next day.
cards.source_title: NC State Ring
cards.access_notes: For class-ring recipients; dates and registration details are provided by the Student Alumni Association.

cards.title: Join Red and White Week
cards.subtitle: NC State’s annual homecoming celebration
cards.notes: Use the annual schedule to choose a campus event, wear red and white, and connect it with the homecoming football game.
cards.short_summary: A weeklong homecoming tradition that brings students and alumni together.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State describes Red and White Week as its annual homecoming celebration and a tradition uniting generations of the Wolfpack.
cards.source_title: Red and White Week
cards.access_notes: Scheduled annually in late October; individual events may have separate registration or ticket requirements.

cards.title: Learn “The Red and White Song”
cards.subtitle: NC State traditional song
cards.notes: Read the official lyrics before a game or campus gathering, then join the song when it is led by the Wolfpack community.
cards.short_summary: A traditional NC State song centered on the university’s red-and-white identity.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Athletics lists “The Red and White Song” among the university’s traditional songs.
cards.source_title: NC State Colors & Songs
cards.access_notes: Commonly associated with Wolfpack events; follow venue entry and event rules.

cards.title: Sing the NC State Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Traditional Wolfpack song
cards.notes: Save the official lyrics before attending a game, then join the Alma Mater when it is performed after the event.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial song performed after NC State games.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State’s Global Training Initiative says the Alma Mater is a traditional vocal tune played after each game.
cards.source_title: How To Sound Like a Wolfpack Football Fan
cards.access_notes: Game attendance may require a ticket; lyrics are publicly available from NC State.

cards.title: Spot Tuffy III at a Wolfpack Event
cards.subtitle: NC State’s Tamaskan live mascot
cards.notes: Watch official athletics event information for appearances, and give Tuffy space while staff manage the live-mascot encounter.
cards.short_summary: Tuffy III continues NC State’s modern live-mascot tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Athletics identifies Tuffy III as the university’s live mascot and dates the modern live-mascot tradition to 2010.
cards.source_title: Tuffy III
cards.access_notes: Appearances are event-dependent; follow staff instructions and do not approach without permission.

cards.entity_name: Howling Cow Ice Cream at the North Carolina State Fair
cards.title: Find Howling Cow at the State Fair
cards.subtitle: NC State dairy tradition at the North Carolina State Fair
cards.notes: When attending the fair, look for NC State’s dairy offering and connect the treat with the university’s long-running ice-cream history.
cards.short_summary: NC State ice cream has been a State Fair tradition since the 1970s.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State University Libraries reports that NC State ice cream has been a State Fair tradition for visitors since the 1970s.
cards.source_title: A Legen-dairy History of Ice Cream on Campus
cards.access_notes: State Fair admission and food purchases are required; availability follows the fair schedule.

boards.school_name: North Carolina State University at Raleigh
boards.title: Your First Weekend at North Carolina State University at Raleigh, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence of named NC State landmarks and student spaces for getting oriented across Main and Centennial campuses.

cards.title: Start at Talley Student Union
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Main Campus
cards.notes: Use the second-floor Information Desk to get oriented, then choose a lounge or terrace for a short reset before continuing your campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for campus information, seating and student-life resources.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State identifies Talley Student Union as the hub of student life and says its second-floor Information Desk assists visitors.
cards.source_title: Talley Student Union
cards.access_notes: Check the Student Centers page for current building hours; the Information Desk is on Talley’s second floor.

cards.title: Meet the wolves at Wolf Plaza
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Near Talley Student Union
cards.notes: Pause by the three bronze wolf sculptures, take a group photo, then use the nearby tunnel as the next waypoint on your Main Campus loop.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor plaza with three bronze wolf sculptures near Talley.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Student Centers says Wolf Plaza features a trio of bronze wolf sculptures by artist Michael Stutz and sits near the Free Expression Tunnel.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Spaces | NC State Student Centers
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; continue on to the nearby Free Expression Tunnel.

cards.title: Walk through the Free Expression Tunnel
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • North–Central Campus connection
cards.notes: Walk through to see the current layers of public paint. If you plan to add anything, review university guidance and bring only permitted materials.
cards.short_summary: A designated graffiti-friendly underpass linking north and central campuses.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Wellness describes the Free Expression Tunnel as a heavily trafficked underpass connecting north and central campuses and a graffiti-friendly zone.
cards.source_title: Outdoor spaces | Wolfpack Wellness
cards.access_notes: This is an active pedestrian underpass; be considerate of people passing through.

cards.title: Cross University Plaza, the Brickyard
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon • North Campus
cards.notes: Use the open plaza as a landmark for your first route across North Campus, and look for posted student-organization tables or campus events.
cards.short_summary: The Brickyard is University Plaza, a North Campus gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Parents and Families Services identifies the Brickyard’s official name as University Plaza and describes it as a gathering spot for students, organizations, club fairs and events.
cards.source_title: Learn the Lingo | NC State Parents and Families Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; event tables and programming vary by day.

cards.title: Stop at the Memorial Belltower
cards.subtitle: Friday near sunset • Henry Square
cards.notes: Take in the memorial’s plaques and architecture from Henry Square. Return another evening if the university announces a red-light celebration.
cards.short_summary: A campus memorial and longstanding rallying point for the Wolfpack community.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State says the Memorial Belltower has been a university symbol and memorial since its 1937 completion, as well as a rallying point for the campus community.
cards.source_title: Belltower Celebrations | Office of the Chancellor
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial area; lighting occasions are announced by the university.

cards.title: Take a breather on the Court of North Carolina
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • North Campus
cards.notes: Choose a bench or patch of grass for coffee, a book or conversation, then identify the older academic buildings that border this large green space.
cards.short_summary: A major Main Campus lawn framed by historic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State Student Centers identifies the Court of North Carolina as the largest green space on Main Campus.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Spaces | NC State Student Centers
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; scheduled events may affect portions of the lawn.

cards.title: Find your D. H. Hill Jr. Library nook
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday • Main Campus
cards.notes: Walk through the Learning Commons and stacks, then save a study-room option for later once you know the library’s current access and reservation rules.
cards.short_summary: A Main Campus library with study rooms, creative technology and a popular-reading lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State University Libraries says Hill Library has reservable study rooms, making and digital-media spaces, and a Popular Reading Lounge in the first-floor Learning Commons.
cards.source_title: D. H. Hill Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s live hours and any access requirements before entering or reserving a room.

cards.title: See Reynolds Coliseum from Talley’s edge
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • Central Campus
cards.notes: Walk by the exterior and read the setting as part of campus history; check the official athletics calendar separately before planning around an event.
cards.short_summary: A Hallowed Place that remains home to NC State women’s basketball.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State News identifies Reynolds Coliseum as a Hallowed Place and says it continues to serve as the home of the university’s women’s basketball team.
cards.source_title: Discover Our Colorful Campus | NC State News
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is a reliable stop; event and interior access depend on the current schedule.

cards.title: Head to Hunt Library on Centennial Campus
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon • Centennial Campus
cards.notes: Explore the public-facing library spaces and its bookBot setting, then pick one collaborative or quiet area to bookmark for a future study session.
cards.short_summary: Centennial Campus’s social and academic hub, with collaborative and quiet study options.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State University Libraries describes Hunt Library as Centennial Campus’s social and academic hub, with bookBot, collaborative spaces and quiet places to study.
cards.source_title: James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s live hours and current access guidance before making the trip to Centennial Campus.

cards.title: Close the weekend at The Oval
cards.subtitle: Sunday late afternoon • Centennial Campus
cards.notes: Finish with a slow lap around the grassy space, noting the Hunt Library and engineering buildings that frame this designated Hallowed Place.
cards.short_summary: A Centennial Campus green space surrounded by engineering buildings and Hunt Library.
cards.evidence_claim: NC State says The Oval is a grassy Centennial Campus space surrounded by four engineering buildings and Hunt Library, and was named the university’s 10th Hallowed Place.
cards.source_title: The Oval Becomes NC State's Newest Hallowed Place | NC State News
cards.access_notes: Outdoor green space on Centennial Campus.
